title: The Major System
tagline: A code in which every digit is a sound. Learn ten sounds and any number can be spoken as words, and then seen.
card: The professional's way to turn numbers into words: ten consonant sounds, free vowels, and a picture for every pair of digits.
goal: you will learn the ten consonant sounds of the Major System, turn two-digit and four-digit numbers into words, and read words back into numbers.

left_off.q: In the shape system, what are 2, 4 and 8?
left_off.a: A swan, a sailboat and a snowman.

left_off.q: In the rhyme system, what are 3, 5 and 7?
left_off.a: A tree, a hive and heaven.

left_off.q: What is the weakness of both systems?
left_off.a: They need one picture per digit, so long numbers become long strings of pictures.

story.heading: Four digits and a locked door

text: You are standing outside a rented flat at eleven at night, and the door has a keypad. The owner wrote the code on a card, and you have just watched the card blow out of your hand into the canal. The owner's phone is switched off. You are quite sure the code was four digits. It might have begun with an eight.
You can see the card in your mind: black ink, a very ordinary number. But you did not turn it into anything. It was just four digits, and four digits are very easy to let go.

check.q: Why can't you remember the door code?
check.a: You never turned it into a picture or word. It stayed as four meaningless digits.

parts.talk: What numbers do you have in your head right now: phone numbers, codes, dates? Which ones do you remember, and why?

text: The idea that fixes it is old. In 1634 a French mathematician, Pierre Hérigone, published a huge textbook in Paris and included in it a code that let letters stand for digits, so that a number could be read as a word. Over the next two centuries others improved it. In the nineteenth century a Polish army officer living in Britain, Major Beniowski, lectured on it; some writers connect his rank with the system's name.

By the twentieth century the code had become the standard way of turning numbers into words. People call it the Major System, and it is the base for most of the number methods you will meet in the rest of this wing.

check.a: A code in which each digit stands for a consonant sound, so that numbers can be turned into words.

parts.talk: Why do you think this idea has survived for four hundred years?

text: The key idea is surprisingly small. Do not give each digit a picture; give each digit a sound. Ten digits, ten sounds. Then any number becomes a string of sounds, and you fill the gaps with vowels, which are free, to make a real word.

The word tie contains one consonant sound, t, so it means 1. Moon has m and n, so it means 32. Once you have a word, you can see it, put it in a scene and keep it. When you need the number back, you read the consonants. The door code that blew away would be a few seconds' work.

check.a: Vowels (and w, h, y) carry no number, so you can add them to make real words out of consonant sounds.

parts.talk: Try it: how would you turn the number 32 into a word? What picture does it make?

words.m: a speech sound made by stopping or narrowing the breath, like t, n or m. Not a, e, i, o or u.
a speech sound like a, e, i, o, u, made with an open mouth. In this system vowels are free.
to do with sounds. A phonetic code goes by how a word sounds, not how it is spelled.
not pronounced. The k in knee is silent.
a system of signs that stands for something else.
to turn a code back into the original. Decode the word into digits.

source: Hérigone's code appears in his Cursus mathematicus (Paris, 1634). The history is told here briefly and in our own words.

method.x: Each digit stands for one consonant sound. Learn the ten and you can say any number as a word.

head: Digit
Sound
Why it fits
rows: Zero begins with a z sound.
A printed t has one downstroke.
The word four ends with r.
L is the Roman numeral for 50, and a hand held up with the thumb out makes an L.
A reversed 6 looks like a j.
A handwritten f looks like an 8.
A 9 is a mirror image of p.

items: Sounds, not spelling. Knee is n (2). Phone is f-n (82). Judge is j-j (66). Cake is k-k (77).
Vowels, w, h and y are free. They carry no number. Use them to build words.
A doubled letter counts once when you hear one sound. Hammer is h-m-r: 34 (m once).
Soft and hard letters follow the sound. City starts with s (0); cat starts with k (7).

method.title: Encode 1066
lines: A judge sits on a throne made of giant toes, which wiggle and tickle him, so he laughs and drops his gavel.
method.pic: A judge on a throne made of huge wiggling toes, laughing so hard that he drops his gavel, while Norman soldiers march past.

method.title: Encode 1776
lines: 17 → TACK (or DOG, DECK). 76 → CAGE (or CASH, COACH).
A giant tack pins a cage to the sky, and the cage is full of bank notes, hundreds of them pouring out.
method.pic: A giant tack pinning a swinging cage to the sky while bank notes pour out of it.

method.x: Decoding is the same thing the other way. Moon has m and n: 3 and 2, so 32. Bike has b and k: 97. Wolf has l and f (the w is free): 58. Tree has t and r: 14.

sounds, not letters.
vowels are free.
that is all.
Choosing words is the creative part. For 10 you can pick toes, tux, dice, daisy. Choose the most vivid one for you. In the next rooms you will build a full list from 00 to 99.
Say the ten digit sounds aloud, in order, and say your own word for the numbers 11, 22 and 33.

try.title: The code
try.prompt: Type the sound for each digit.

try.title: Decode these words
try.prompt: Match each word to its number.

try.title: Encode 1945
try.prompt: 1945 (the end of the Second World War). Split it into 19 and 45. Find consonant sounds, make two words and put them in a vivid scene.
try.model: 19 = t/d + p/b: TUB or TAPE. 45 = r + l: RAIL or ROLE. A huge tub sits on a railway line, and soldiers are throwing their uniforms into it and dancing out as the train goes through.
checks: My two words contain the right sounds.
The two words are in one vivid scene.

try.title: Encode 1969
try.prompt: 1969 (the Moon landing). Split into 19 and 69 and make a scene.
try.model: 19 = TAPE (t, p). 69 = SHIP (sh, p) or CHIP. A huge ship is wrapped in sticky tape, floating up into space, the crew taping flags to the stars.

try.title: A number of your own
try.prompt: Pick a four-digit number you need (a year of birth, a code, part of a phone number). Split into two pairs. Write the sounds, the words and the scene.
try.model: There is no single answer. Check that every consonant sound in each word matches a digit, and that the vowels are the only free letters.
checks: Each consonant sound matches the digit.
I used free vowels to make real words.

try.q: Which number does the word KNIFE spell?
try.why: Knife is n (2) and f (8), and the k, i, e are silent or free: 28.

try.title: Say it fast
try.prompt: Say the digit sounds, from 0 to 9, as quickly as you can. Then say them backwards. Repeat twice.

cards: j, sh, ch, soft g (a reversed 6 looks like j)
k, hard g (two 7s make a k)
f, v (a written f looks like 8)
p, b (a 9 is a mirror p)

quiz.q: What number does the word SUN stand for?

quiz.why: 6 is j, sh, ch or soft g.

quiz.q: Which letters are free in the Major System?
quiz.why: The vowels, w, h and y carry no number.

quiz.q: How do you decode the word PHONE?
opts: By sounds: f and n, so 82
quiz.why: PH is an f sound (8) and n is 2: 82.

challenge.title: Memory challenge: four years as words
challenge.intro: These eight words encode 1066, 1776, 1945 and 1989: toes judge | tack cage | tub rail | tap fib. Learn them in order as a story, then type them. Afterwards, decode them back to digits.
challenge.study: Make one story of the eight words. Toes and a judge; a tack and a cage; a tub and a rail; a tap and a fib.

look_back.q: In the shape system, what is 6? And in the rhyme system?
Why is a number hard to remember?
look_back.a: A number is not a picture, so the mind has nothing to hold on to.

look_back.q: Why should each link in a chain involve only two items?
look_back.a: Each link is a simple picture of two things interacting; the chain is made of overlapping pairs.
Using places (loci) in a fixed route to store pictures in order.
